110	\section{Profiling Resolution and Stability}
111	\label{sec:profiling_resolution}
112	
113	We compare standard-resolution profiling (16 sequences $\times$ 512 tokens) against high-resolution profiling (64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens) on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression.
114	
115	High-resolution profiling improves constrained MCKP from 11.23 to 10.91 PPL ($-$0.32 absolute).
116	Relative to the bf16 baseline (9.81), this reduces the degradation from 1.42 to 1.10, a 22.5\% reduction.
117	The improvement comes from finer-grained sensitivity estimates: standard profiling detects non-zero 2-bit distortion in 37 of 112 heads, while high-resolution profiling detects 100 of 112 (2.7$\times$ more).
118	
119	The additional signal changes 8 of 112 head assignments.
120	High-resolution profiling protects shallow layers (L1--L3) at higher bit-widths while compressing mid-layers (L5--L11) more aggressively---a redistribution that standard profiling misses because its distortion estimates for these heads fall below the noise floor.
121	
122	\paragraph{Multi-seed stability.}
123	The profiled allocation is stable across calibration subsets.
124	Under hires profiling on Qwen2.5-7B, constrained MCKP yields mean PPL $10.99 \pm 0.06$ across 3 random calibration seeds (individual runs: 11.02, 10.90, 11.05), with std/mean below 0.6\%.
125	The bit distribution is identical across all seeds ($\{$2-bit: 8, 4-bit: 100, 8-bit: 4$\}$), and 101 of 112 heads (90.2\%) receive the same assignment in all three runs.
126	This stability confirms that the per-head sensitivity ranking is robust to calibration sampling noise.
127	
128	\paragraph{Numerical precision.}
129	Float32 profiling (64 $\times$ 2048 tokens) yields an identical constrained allocation and PPL within seed variance (10.89 vs.\ 10.91, $\Delta = 0.02 < \sigma = 0.06$), confirming that bfloat16 precision is sufficient for the profiling step.
130	
131	\paragraph{Per-layer optimality.}
132	To validate the additive distortion assumption underlying the MCKP formulation, we compare constrained MCKP against a per-layer brute-force oracle that exhaustively enumerates all $4^4 = 256$ bit-width combinations within each 4-head group on Qwen2.5-7B (hires profiling).

134	All three gaps involve repositioning a 2-bit assignment among heads with near-identical sensitivity within the same layer bit budget.
135	The negligible total gap ($<0.04$ PPL) confirms that the per-head additive distortion model closely approximates the true layer-level interaction.

## 1. 可支持的 claim 强度

如果 4 模型 × 3 seed 全部显示 |constrained − uniform| < seed std:

**最强可辩护的表述**（推荐）：
"The absence of MCKP benefit on non-spread models is confirmed across 3 independent calibration seeds per model (std < 0.1 PPL), ruling out calibration-specific artifacts. - "statistically significant null result" — 需要 formal hypothesis test（t-test / equivalence test）
- "proven equivalent to uniform" — 等价性需要 TOST (two one-sided t-test) 才能形式化

**可以 claim**：
- "null results are reproducible across calibration seeds" ✓
- "the lack of benefit is not a seed-dependent artifact" ✓
- "profiling noise (~0.06 PPL) is negligible relative to Qwen's signal (4.5 PPL)" ✓

## 2. 如果 non-Qwen std ≈ 0.05-0.1

关键推论：Qwen 的 29.4% 改善 = 4.54 PPL 绝对值，是 profiling noise (0.06) 的 **75×**。non-spread 模型的 |constrained − uniform| < 0.03 PPL，远低于 noise floor。这支持：

"The diagnostic rule's predictions are not resolution-limited: Qwen's benefit (4.54 PPL) exceeds profiling noise by 75×, while non-spread models' null deltas (< 0.03 PPL) lie below the noise floor—confirming that the absence of benefit reflects genuine sensitivity uniformity, not insufficient profiling resolution."

## 3. 论文位置建议

**推荐 (c) + (a) 组合**：
- 主文 experiments.tex: 在 line 69 (Qwen multi-seed) 后加 1-2 句概括 non-spread 结果："Non-spread models confirm seed independence: Llama 8.47±X, Mistral 7.13±Y, with constrained-uniform gap below seed std in all cases (Appendix~\ref{sec:profiling_resolution})."
- Appendix §profiling_resolution: 新增一张小表（4 model × seed mean/std/uniform）并列于 Qwen 的 multi-seed 段落之后

**不推荐 (b)**：Table 1 已经 9 rows × 5 cols，加 ±std 列会过于拥挤且对 non-spread 模型意义不大（std of what？constrained ≈ uniform ≈ same number）。

W2 concern: "null results lack multi-seed confirmation"

- **Llama (Spike) + Mistral (Flat) 完成** → **80% 解决**。覆盖两种 non-spread pattern，加上 Qwen (Spread) 已有 3 seed = 全部三种 pattern 有 multi-seed。

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related_work}

\paragraph{KV Cache Quantization.}
Uniform-precision methods quantize the KV cache at a single bit-width across all heads, using techniques such as asymmetric per-channel/per-token schemes~\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant}, quantization--serving co-design~\cite{lin2024qserve}, salient-token identification~\cite{he2024zipcache}, low-rank plus sparse correction~\cite{kang2024gear}, sliding-window adaptation~\cite{duanmu2024skvq}, rotation-based outlier smoothing for robust 2-bit~\cite{su2025rotatekv}, 2-bit with adaptive token retention~\cite{sharma2025minikv}, and adapter-based inter-layer prediction at 2--2.5 bits~\cite{shutova2025aquakv}.
We extend the design space to per-head non-uniform allocation over hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$.
Our per-head bit-width allocation is orthogonal to per-channel quantization schemes such as KIVI: KIVI determines \emph{how} each head is quantized (asymmetric per-channel scaling), while our method determines \emph{at what precision} (bit-width selection across heads).
The two can be composed, though the per-channel method dominates when available (\S\ref{sec:main_results}); per-head allocation provides independent value in symmetric-only environments where per-channel asymmetric quantization is unavailable.
QAQ~\cite{dong2024qaq} also pursues mixed-precision KV cache but selects precision dynamically at inference time using attention scores; in contrast, our allocation is determined offline via one-shot profiling and enforces a cardinality constraint that prevents compounding---a failure mode that any unconstrained adaptive scheme remains susceptible to.

\paragraph{KV Cache Eviction.}
Complementary to quantization, eviction methods reduce cache size by discarding tokens---retaining heavy-hitters~\cite{zhang2023h2o}, per-head important tokens~\cite{li2024snapkv,ge2024fastgen}, persistent-importance tokens~\cite{liu2024scissorhands}, attention sinks~\cite{xiao2024streamingllm}, or progressively fewer tokens in deeper layers~\cite{yang2024pyramidinfer}.
Recent per-head eviction methods allocate non-uniform budgets across heads based on retrieval-vs-reasoning importance~\cite{fu2025headkv} or adaptive optimization extending SnapKV/PyramidKV~\cite{feng2025adakv}, confirming that head-level heterogeneity is exploitable for eviction; our work shows it is equally exploitable for quantization.


\paragraph{Mixed-Precision Quantization (Weights).}
Mixed-precision allocation has a long history at the weight level.
HAWQ~\cite{dong2019hawq} and HAWQ-V2~\cite{dong2020hawqv2} use second-order (Hessian-based) sensitivity to assign per-layer bit-widths, with V2 introducing block-wise trace-weighted scoring and Pareto-frontier selection; HAQ~\cite{wang2019haq} learns an allocation by reinforcement learning under hardware-aware latency/energy constraints.
These methods operate on weights, where per-layer distortions are approximately additive and sensitivity varies smoothly across layers.
KV cache quantization presents a qualitatively different challenge: 2-bit head distortions compound super-additively through the residual stream (\S\ref{sec:compounding}), a phenomenon absent in weight quantization where each layer's parameters are independently quantized.
Notably, AQLM~\cite{egiazarian2024aqlm} and QuIP\#~\cite{tseng2024quipsharp} have observed non-additive error behaviour in extreme weight quantization when codebook interactions amplify distortion beyond per-parameter predictions; we independently identify an analogous phenomenon in per-head KV cache allocation, where co-activating multiple 2-bit heads triggers super-additive degradation through the residual stream.
Our primary contribution is not the allocation algorithm itself---any MCKP or greedy solver suffices---but the diagnosis and fix of this compounding effect via cardinality constraints, and the characterization of when non-uniform allocation is beneficial (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).

\paragraph{Mixed-Precision Rate-Distortion Allocation.}
RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formulates per-head bit-width selection as an MCKP and proves greedy optimality for consecutive bit-widths $\{2,\ldots,6\}$ via the polymatroid structure, which relies on the assumption that per-head distortions decompose additively into the global objective---valid when adjacent bit-widths differ by a single bit so that quantization noise stays in the small-perturbation regime.
On hardware-aligned $\{2,4,8,16\}$, the 4$\times$ gap between 2-bit and 4-bit drives 2-bit distortion to compound super-additively, breaking the polymatroid structure and the additivity assumption with it.
Concretely, running RateQuant's greedy algorithm (Algorithm~1) directly on $\{2,4,8,16\}$ yields 32.45 PPL on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression---catastrophically worse than uniform 4-bit (15.45)---whereas our cardinality constraint on simultaneously active 2-bit heads recovers 10.91 PPL at the same average bit-width.
The constraint is the minimal fix that restores the additive regime in which RateQuant's polymatroid argument applies.
Related mixed-precision KV-cache work operates at coarser granularity---layer-level via gradient-based sensitivity~\cite{li2025kvmix} or Pareto search over hardware-friendly precision pairs~\cite{li2025kvtuner}, block-level via progressive decoding-step quantization for long-CoT reasoning~\cite{liu2025pmkvq}, channel-level via dynamic precision boost on sensitive Key channels~\cite{xia2025kitty}, token-level via a learned on-device controller~\cite{haeriboroujeni2026dontwaste}, memory-budget-level~\cite{lei2026arkv}---at the weight level~\cite{kim2024squeezellm}, or dynamically at inference time~\cite{zhang2025mixkvq}; our allocation is static and per-head.
KVTuner~\cite{li2025kvtuner} assigns mixed precision at the layer level (all heads within a layer share a single bit-width); our head-level granularity exposes intra-layer heterogeneity at the cost of a combinatorially larger search space, which the cardinality constraint renders tractable.

\paragraph{Attention Head Analysis.}
Prior work studies head redundancy and pruning~\cite{voita2019analyzing,michel2019sixteen}, focusing on which heads can be removed entirely.
Our analysis asks a different question: which heads are sensitive to \emph{quantization}, and how heterogeneous that sensitivity is across architectures---a property that determines whether non-uniform allocation is beneficial (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Per-head mixed-precision quantization of the KV cache is a natural strategy for reducing memory during LLM inference: assign fewer bits to insensitive heads and more bits to sensitive ones, achieving lower perplexity than uniform quantization at the same average bit-width.
Recent work on KV cache quantization explores both uniform schemes~\cite{liu2024kivi,hooper2024kvquant,lin2024qserve,he2024zipcache} and token-level mixed-precision approaches~\cite{ge2024fastgen,lei2026arkv}, while complementary methods reduce cache size through eviction~\cite{zhang2023h2o,li2024snapkv}.
RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalizes per-head allocation as a rate-distortion optimization and shows that greedy allocation is optimal when bit-widths are consecutive integers $\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, exploiting the polymatroid structure of the feasible set (their Proposition~6).

In practice, hardware-efficient inference requires bit-widths drawn from $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$---the formats natively supported by modern accelerators.
On this non-consecutive set, the polymatroid structure breaks down, and greedy is no longer provably optimal.
One might expect that exact MCKP solvers would fill this gap.
They do not.
On Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression, unconstrained greedy achieves 32.45 PPL and unconstrained MCKP achieves 36.92---both \emph{far worse} than uniform 4-bit (15.45).
The optimization does not merely underperform; it fails catastrophically.

The issue traces not to solver suboptimality but to a violation of the additive distortion assumption.
Both solvers assign 68--75 of 112 KV heads to 2-bit, where per-head quantization errors compound through the residual stream.
The additive model predicts $\sim$11 PPL; the actual PPL is $3$--$4\times$ higher, because 2-bit distortions are orders of magnitude larger than 4-bit and compound super-linearly when many heads are quantized simultaneously.

This observation points to a minimal intervention: cap the number of 2-bit assignments.
We add a single cardinality constraint $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h{=}2] \leq k$ to the standard MCKP formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}).
On Qwen2.5-7B, setting $k{=}8$ (7\% of heads) yields 10.91 PPL---a 29.4\% reduction over uniform 4-bit.
The constraint works by forcing the solver to use 2-bit only on the least-sensitive heads, while redistributing the freed budget to protect sensitive heads at 8-bit or 16-bit.
This is not a heuristic patch: the constraint directly addresses the identified failure mode and is compatible with any solver.
The constraint is beneficial even on flat-distribution architectures: on Gemma-2-9B, unconstrained MCKP assigns 31.5\% of heads to 2-bit, producing a moderate $1.47\times$ degradation; the constraint reduces this to within 0.5\% of uniform.

A surprising consequence is that the cardinality constraint renders solver choice irrelevant.
Constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations across all tested architectures (112/112 heads on Qwen, 256/256 on Llama, 255/256 on Mistral), enabling practitioners to use the simpler $O(H \log H)$ greedy algorithm.
A per-layer brute-force oracle confirms near-optimality: the maximum gap is 0.02 PPL, 0.4\% of the total improvement (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).

However, non-uniform allocation does not help universally.
On the remaining eight models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where the $3.4\times$ increase in head count dilutes spread into flat---constrained MCKP provides no meaningful improvement.
The difference traces to the \emph{distribution shape} of head sensitivity, not GQA ratio or model scale alone: Qwen-7B's Layer-0 heads form a cluster of high sensitivity across multiple bitwidths (``spread''); Yi-1.5, CodeLlama, and Llama have dominant outliers (``spike''); Gemma-2, Mistral, Phi-3-medium, Qwen-14B, and Pythia show near-uniform or diluted sensitivity (``flat'').

This motivates a question prior work does not address: \emph{when} should a practitioner use per-head mixed-precision quantization?
We propose a joint empirical decision rule based on concentration and distribution shape (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}) that correctly classifies all nine models (9/9), including a within-family scale contrast.
Yi-1.5 is a critical test: its concentration ($0.71$) exceeds Qwen-7B's, but its single-outlier spike has no cross-bitwidth gradient, so MCKP cannot redistribute budget.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item We identify 2-bit distortion compounding as a major contributing factor in the degradation observed under unconstrained per-head KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths, and show that a single cardinality constraint on 2-bit assignments suffices to prevent it, reducing Qwen2.5-7B PPL from 32--37 (unconstrained) to 10.91 (constrained) at $4\times$ compression (\S\ref{sec:compounding}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}).

\item RateQuant~\cite{zuo2026ratequant} formalized per-head MCKP and proved greedy optimality for consecutive integer bit-widths. Our algorithmic contribution is a single cardinality constraint (Eq.~\ref{eq:constraint}); the scientific contribution is the systematic finding that this constraint suffices to prevent compounding, yet eight of nine tested models do not benefit from non-uniform allocation---the constraint renders solver choice irrelevant, with constrained greedy and MCKP producing equivalent allocations across all tested architectures (\S\ref{sec:solver_equiv}).

\item We provide an empirical characterization of head sensitivity heterogeneity across nine models, revealing three distribution shapes (spread, spike, flat) that predict allocation benefit. Concentration and $t_1/t_5$ ratio correctly classify all nine models (9/9), though the spread pattern is observed in only one model ($N{=}1$, Qwen2.5-7B); the suggested thresholds should be treated as preliminary (\S\ref{sec:heterogeneity}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}

\subsection{Heterogeneity Characterization}
\label{sec:heterogeneity}

The benefit of non-uniform allocation depends on how unevenly head sensitivities are distributed.
We quantify this with a \emph{top-5\% concentration metric}: sort per-head 2-bit distortions $d_h(2)$ in descending order and compute the fraction of total distortion contributed by the top 5\% of heads.
High concentration indicates that a few heads are disproportionately sensitive; low concentration indicates near-uniform sensitivity.

Table~\ref{tab:heterogeneity} summarizes the results across nine models at $4\times$ compression.
The central finding is that MCKP benefit requires \emph{spread heterogeneity}---multiple heads with cross-bitwidth sensitivity gradients---rather than sensitivity concentrated in a single outlier at one bitwidth.

Qwen2.5-7B exemplifies the spread pattern (top-5\% concentration 0.61, $t_1/t_5{=}0.57$), with Layer-0 heads contributing the majority of total 2-bit distortion across multiple bitwidths.
Constrained MCKP reduces degradation from $+$5.64 PPL (uniform) to $+$1.10 PPL, a 29.4\% improvement over uniform 4-bit. %exp_id=qwen_constrained_mckp

Yi-1.5-9B is a critical counterexample: despite high concentration ($0.71$, exceeding Qwen's $0.61$), constrained MCKP matches uniform ($+$0.20 vs.\ $+$0.20). %exp_id=yi15_hires_constrained_mckp
Yi-1.5's sensitivity is dominated by a single extreme outlier: Layer-4 Head-3 ($d_h(2){=}13.12$, second-ranked head: $0.55$, a $24\times$ gap; $t_1/t_5{=}0.90$). %exp_id=yi15_hires_profiling
Critically, L4H3's 4-bit and 8-bit deltas are ${\approx}\,0$, so upgrading it from 2-bit to 4-bit removes the distortion, but budget freed by downgrading other heads has nowhere useful to go---a ``spike'' pattern with sensitivity at only one bitwidth.
In contrast, Qwen's Layer-0 heads exhibit non-zero deltas at multiple bitwidths (e.g., L0H0: 2-bit delta ${=}6.74$, with positive 4-bit and 8-bit deltas), giving the solver a multi-bitwidth gradient across several heads---a ``spread'' pattern enabling meaningful reallocation. %exp_id=qwen_hires_profiling

Llama-3.1-8B has concentration $0.57$---comparable to Qwen's $0.61$---yet its spike pattern ($t_1/t_5{=}0.85$), dominated by a single head (L2H5), yields allocation indistinguishable from uniform ($+$0.36 vs.\ $+$0.38), demonstrating that concentration alone is insufficient without spread structure. %exp_id=llama_hires_bf16_2bitonly %exp_id=llama_hires_constrained
CodeLlama-7B reinforces this: the highest concentration tested ($0.80$) with an extreme spike ($t_1/t_5{=}0.81$, L1H1 contributes $81\%$ of top-5 delta, $11.3\times$ the second-ranked head) yields no benefit when dominated by a single outlier; constrained MCKP ($k{=}2$) confirms: $+$0.17 vs.\ uniform $+$0.19, consistent with a near-uniform allocation (1021/1024 heads at 4-bit). %exp_id=codellama_constrained_mckp
Mistral-7B-v0.3 ($t_1/t_5{=}0.41$) and Gemma-2-9B ($t_1/t_5{=}0.38$) both exhibit flat distributions with low concentration ($0.24$ and $0.23$), leaving no reliable signal; constrained MCKP is slightly worse than uniform in both cases ($+$0.13 vs.\ $+$0.10 for Mistral; $+$0.16 vs.\ $+$0.14 for Gemma-2). %exp_id=mistral_c4_cross_dataset %exp_id=gemma2_full_pipeline

Pythia-1.4B extends the evaluation to MHA (1:1 ratio, 384 heads).
Low concentration ($0.24$) and $t_1/t_5{=}0.28$ place it in the flat category; constrained MCKP confirms this ($+$7.96 vs.\ uniform $+$7.80, $+$0.7\%). %exp_id=pythia14b_constrained_pipeline

Phi-3-medium-14B (GQA 4:1, 400 heads) has the lowest concentration in our test set ($0.17$) with $t_1/t_5{=}0.23$; the joint rule classifies it as flat, confirmed by evaluation (constrained $+$0.18 vs.\ uniform $+$0.16 PPL).
Although $t_1/t_5$ is low (indicating no dominant outlier), the concentration of 0.17 places the cumulative top-5\% delta below the level required for meaningful reallocation---spread structure without sufficient absolute magnitude does not create optimization opportunities. %exp_id=phi3_medium_hires_profiling_v2 %exp_id=phi3_medium_constrained_mckp

\paragraph{Scale-dependent concentration dilution.}
Qwen2.5-14B (GQA 5:1, 384 heads) provides a within-family comparison: $t_1/t_5$ is similar (0.57 vs.\ 0.68), but concentration drops from 0.61 (7B) to 0.33 (14B)---diluted by $3.4\times$ more heads into the flat regime.
Sensitivity is dominated by a single head (L0H5, $d_h(2){=}1.845$; second-ranked: $0.237$, a $7.8\times$ gap), but 384 heads dilute cumulative signal below the concentration threshold.
Concentration, not within-head structure, is thus the primary discriminator: the rule correctly identifies Qwen-7B as the single model$\times$scale combination where non-uniform allocation helps.

\centering
\small
\caption{Head sensitivity heterogeneity and constrained allocation benefit at $4\times$ compression. $t_1/t_5$: ratio of the most sensitive head's 2-bit distortion to the sum of the top-5\% of heads' distortions (low${=}$spread, high${=}$spike); the percentage threshold ensures comparability across models with different head counts (112--400). $^*$BOS-corrected.}

The per-head heatmap (Figure~\ref{fig:heatmap}, Appendix~\ref{sec:heatmap_appendix}) confirms this visually: Qwen's Layer-0 heads show high distortion while mid-to-deep layers are near-zero (spread); Yi-1.5 shows a single bright spot at Layer-4 Head-3 (64\% of total delta) with the remaining 191 heads near-uniform (spike); Gemma-2 and Mistral show uniformly low distortion.

\subsection{Empirical Decision Rule}
\label{sec:diagnostic}

MCKP benefit requires not just high concentration but a specific \emph{shape}---spread heterogeneity across multiple heads with cross-bitwidth sensitivity gradients.
This motivates a joint empirical decision rule for deciding when non-uniform allocation is worthwhile.
Given the profiling results from \S\ref{sec:profiling}, compute the top-5\% concentration and $t_1/t_5$ ratio, then select:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
\item \textbf{Spread} (concentration $\geq 0.50$ \emph{and} $t_1/t_5 \leq 0.70$): non-uniform recommended. Qwen-7B (0.61, $t_1/t_5{=}0.57$): $-$29.4\% PPL.
\item \textbf{Spike} ($t_1/t_5 > 0.70$ \emph{and} concentration $\geq 0.25$): use uniform. A dominant outlier with no cross-bitwidth gradient cannot be exploited. Yi-1.5 (0.71, 0.90), CodeLlama (0.80, 0.81), and Llama (0.57, 0.85): no benefit.
\item \textbf{Flat} (concentration $< 0.25$, or concentration $\in [0.25, 0.50)$ with $t_1/t_5 \leq 0.70$): use uniform. Too little cumulative delta for meaningful reallocation. Mistral (0.24), Gemma-2 (0.23), Phi-3-medium (0.17), Qwen-14B (0.33), and Pythia (0.24): no benefit or counterproductive.
\end{itemize}

Both conditions are needed: CodeLlama ($0.80$), Llama ($0.57$), and Yi-1.5 ($0.71$) all exceed the concentration threshold yet show no MCKP benefit; their spike shapes ($t_1/t_5 \geq 0.70$) correctly override.
A concentration-only rule would misclassify all three as spread; $t_1/t_5$ is the critical second discriminator.
The rule is experimentally confirmed on all nine models (9/9), including the within-family scale contrast (Qwen-7B spread vs.\ 14B flat), Pythia-1.4B (MHA, flat), and CodeLlama-7B (MHA, spike).
Only Qwen-7B exhibits the spread pattern ($N{=}1$); the suggested thresholds should be treated as preliminary until confirmed on additional models.
The rule reuses profiling data already required by the solver and adds no overhead.

\paragraph{Why is Qwen-7B the only spread model?}
We offer two non-exclusive hypotheses, both requiring further validation.
First, Qwen-7B's high GQA ratio (7:1) means each KV head aggregates attention from 7 query heads, potentially driving greater functional specialization and thus larger inter-head sensitivity differences.
However, Yi-1.5 (8:1) and Qwen-14B (5:1) have comparable or higher GQA ratios yet do not exhibit spread, so GQA ratio alone is insufficient.
Second, scale-dependent concentration dilution may play a role: Qwen-14B (same architecture family, $3.4\times$ more heads) dilutes into the flat regime despite similar within-head structure ($t_1/t_5$ 0.68 vs.\ 0.57).
This suggests that increasing head count may systematically reduce concentration, making spread less likely at larger scales---a hypothesis consistent with the Qwen-7B/14B contrast but requiring evaluation on additional model families and scales.

On Qwen-7B, a simple L0-protection heuristic with random downgrade captures 93\% of the MCKP benefit under standard-resolution profiling (median PPL 11.52 vs MCKP 11.23), suggesting that identifying which heads to \emph{protect} matters more than the optimization algorithm---consistent with our solver-equivalence finding.

Additional analyses---granularity tradeoff (Appendix~\ref{sec:granularity}), aggressive compression, profiling resolution and stability, per-layer optimality, and KV separation---are in Appendices~\ref{sec:granularity}--\ref{sec:kv_separation}.

% TODO(kivi-compounding): If KIVI compounding persists, add discussion of
% quantization-scheme independence here. If disappears, add scoping discussion.

Across nine models spanning 1.4B--14B parameters and seven architecture families (MHA through GQA 8:1), we find that per-head non-uniform KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned bit-widths $\{2,4,8,16\}$ provides negligible improvement over uniform 4-bit for eight of nine models.
The sole exception is Qwen2.5-7B, where a cardinality-constrained solver achieves 10.91 perplexity at $4\times$ compression---a 29.4\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45)---while unconstrained solvers degrade catastrophically (32--37 PPL) due to 2-bit distortion compounding through the residual stream.
The benefit depends not on GQA ratio or model scale, but on whether sensitivity heterogeneity is \emph{spread} across multiple heads with cross-bitwidth gradients---a pattern observed in only one model ($N{=}1$) in our study.
On the remaining eight models---including Qwen2.5-14B, where scaling dilutes the spread pattern---non-uniform allocation provides no meaningful benefit: Yi-1.5-9B has high concentration (0.71, exceeding Qwen-7B's 0.61) yet gains nothing, because its single-outlier ``spike'' has no cross-bitwidth gradient.
The cardinality constraint prevents catastrophic over-allocation on Qwen-7B and moderate degradation on flat models (Gemma-2: unconstrained $1.47\times$ degradation reduced to within 0.5\% of uniform), while rendering solver choice irrelevant---constrained greedy and MCKP produce identical allocations---enabling a simple $O(H\log H)$ greedy algorithm.
We characterize sensitivity heterogeneity across all nine models using concentration and distribution shape ($t_1/t_5$ ratio), identifying three patterns (spread, spike, flat) that correctly predict allocation benefit (9/9); the thresholds are preliminary, as only one model exhibits the spread pattern.

[severity: info] Method 改进深度分析——理论与实验两端反思

## 一、理论层面：约束本身的最优性

### 1.1 全局 k vs 每层 k

当前方法：全局 cardinality constraint $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h=2] \leq k$。

**问题**：compounding onset 是 architecture-dependent 的（Qwen ~k=32, Llama ~k=64, Mistral ~k=128），但也可能是 layer-dependent 的——Layer 0 的 2-bit heads 可能比 deep layer 的 2-bit heads 更危险（residual stream 早期扰动放大更多层）。

**改进方向**：per-layer cap $k_l$（如 $k_l \leq 2$ per layer）。

**评估**：
- 理论吸引力高——更精细的约束应该不差于全局约束
- 但 solver equivalence 已证明当前 k 下 greedy≡MCKP，且 brute-force oracle gap 仅 0.02 PPL → per-layer 优化的上界极低
- **结论：理论上 sound，但实际收益上界 ≤0.02 PPL，不值得 9 天内投入实验**
- 论文价值：Discussion 中一句话提及即可

### 1.2 Weighted/adaptive k

动态 k（如随 sequence length 变化）或加权约束（不同 head 的 2-bit "代价"不同）。

**评估**：
- 动态 k 需要 inference-time 决策，违背 "static offline allocation" 的核心设计
- 加权约束本质是把约束从 cardinality 升级为 knapsack-within-knapsack → 过度工程化
- **结论：方向正确但超出本文 scope，属于 future work**

### 1.3 非加性 profiling（pairwise interaction）

当前 profiling 假设：单独量化 head h 的 distortion $d_h(b)$ 可独立测量。实际 compounding 说明 heads 之间有交互。

**评估**：
- 完整 pairwise profiling：$O(H^2)$ 次 forward pass（Qwen 112 heads → 6272 次），不可行
- Sampling-based interaction estimation 可行但增加复杂度
- **关键洞察**：L0 heuristic 捕获 87-93% benefit → 交互效应虽存在但主要影响已被 "保护敏感头" 策略覆盖。精确建模交互的边际收益极小
- **结论：理论上是 limitation，论文应在 Limitations 中提及，但不影响实用价值**

## 二、实验层面：Method bottleneck 分析

### 2.1 Qwen 10.91 vs KIVI 9.90 的 gap 来源

数据：KIVI 4-bit = 9.90, 我们的 symmetric MCKP = 10.91, KIVI+MCKP = 9.90（与 KIVI alone 相同）。

**诊断**：
- 1.01 PPL gap **完全来自量化方案**（per-channel asymmetric vs symmetric），不来自 allocation strategy
- KIVI+MCKP = KIVI alone → per-channel 信号**完全 subsumes** per-head allocation 信号
- **这是方法的核心局限**：当 per-channel asymmetric quantization 可用时，per-head allocation 无附加价值

**论文处理**：当前 related_work.tex L6 已正确表述："per-channel method dominates when available; per-head allocation provides independent value in symmetric-only environments"。这是诚实且正确的 positioning。

### 2.2 8/9 models 无 benefit 的根本原因

不是方法缺陷，是**现象本身的性质**：
- Spread pattern (多头跨 bitwidth 梯度) 是 non-uniform allocation 的**必要条件**
- 9 个模型中只有 Qwen-7B 满足 → 这是 architecture/training 的性质，不是 solver 能修复的
- **这是论文最诚实的贡献之一**：系统性地证明了 "when NOT to use" 比盲目推广更有价值

### 2.3 Long-context amplification

长序列可能放大 distortion（更多 KV tokens → attention 累积误差更大）。

**评估**：
- 8K eval 实验已有（Llama/Mistral/InternLM2），但主要验证 uniform 行为
- long-context 下 constraint 是否需要更紧的 k 是未验证的问题
- **9 天内可行性**：需要 long-context MCKP eval（Qwen 8K），~2-4 GPU-hours → **可行但优先级低**

## 三、9 天内可提升论文分数的实验（按优先级）

### Priority 1: KIVI asymmetric compounding（已准备脚本）
- **目标**：验证 constraint 在 KIVI 环境下是否仍有价值（或完全被 subsume）
- **预测**：大概率 KIVI 完全 subsume（基于 KIVI+MCKP = KIVI 数据），但实验确认 = 论文更 robust
- **收益**：如果 constraint 在 KIVI 下仍有边际价值 → 大幅加强 paper；如果无价值 → 论文 positioning 不变（已正确 scoped to symmetric-only）
- **成本**：~8 GPU-hours
- **优先级**：★★★★★（直接回答 reviewer 最可能的攻击点）

### Priority 2: Solver equivalence verify（已准备脚本）
- **目标**：关闭 Llama/Mistral "256/256, 255/256" claim 的验证缺口
- **成本**：~2 GPU-hours
- **优先级**：★★★★（claim 已在论文中，必须有数据支撑）

### Priority 3: Multi-seed completion（已在跑）
- Llama seeds 123+456 ~4-5h, Mistral seeds 123+456 ~5-6h
- 完成后关闭 W2 robustness concern 80%→100%

### Priority 4: Long-context MCKP eval（新实验）
- Qwen-7B 8K sequences 下 constrained MCKP vs uniform
- ~4 GPU-hours
- **收益中等**：如果 long-context 放大 constraint value → 新 selling point；如果不变 → appendix 一行

### Not recommended in 9 days:
- Per-layer k optimization（上界 0.02 PPL）
- Interaction-aware profiling（实现复杂，收益不明）
- Additional model families（N=1 limitation 已诚实声明，加 1-2 个模型不改变结论）

## 四、总结判断

**方法的核心局限是 architectural 的，不是 algorithmic 的**：
1. Per-channel asymmetric quantization subsumes per-head allocation signal
2. Spread pattern 只在 1/9 models 出现

这两点论文已诚实表述。方法改进的空间主要在 "组合 KIVI + constraint 是否有 synergy" 这个问题上——KIVI compounding 实验是唯一能改变 paper story 的实验。其余方向属于 future work 或 diminishing returns。

**建议行动**：GPU 空出后立即提交 KIVI compounding + solver equivalence verify。

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Models.}
We evaluate nine models spanning seven architecture families and diverse attention configurations:
\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA 7:1, 28 layers $\times$ 4 KV heads = 112),
\textbf{Qwen2.5-14B} (GQA 5:1, 48 $\times$ 8 = 384),
\textbf{Yi-1.5-9B} (GQA 8:1, 48 $\times$ 4 = 192),
\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256),
\textbf{CodeLlama-7B}\footnote{CodeLlama multi-bit profiles synthesized from 2-bit-only profiling; classification robust as constrained allocation is dominated by 4-bit heads.} (MHA 1:1, 32 $\times$ 32 = 1024),
\textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (GQA 4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256, sliding window attention),
\textbf{Gemma-2-9B} (GQA 2:1, 42 $\times$ 8 = 336, \texttt{head\_dim}=256, attention logit softcapping),
\textbf{Phi-3-medium-14B} (GQA 4:1, 40 $\times$ 10 = 400),
and \textbf{Pythia-1.4B} (MHA 1:1, 24 $\times$ 16 = 384).
All nine models undergo full constrained evaluation.
This selection spans GQA ratios from 1:1 (MHA) to 8:1 and covers standard, sliding-window, softcapped, and multi-head attention.

\paragraph{Evaluation.}
We report perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.
For downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.

\paragraph{Profiling.}
Per-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.
All results use high-resolution profiling (64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train); Appendix~\ref{sec:profiling_resolution} compares against standard-resolution profiling (16 seq $\times$ 512 tok).

\paragraph{Compression and constraint.}
The default target is 4$\times$ compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio 0.25).
The cardinality constraint limits 2-bit assignments to at most $k$ heads, where $k$ is selected via the compounding sweep described in \S\ref{sec:method} ($k{=}8$ for Qwen-7B and Qwen-14B, $k{=}2$ for Yi-1.5, Llama, CodeLlama, and Mistral, $k{=}8$ for Gemma-2, Phi-3-medium, and Pythia).

\paragraph{Baselines.}
We compare against:
(1)~uniform 4-bit quantization;
(2)~unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style~\cite{zuo2026ratequant});
(3)~unconstrained MCKP allocation;
(4)~an L0-random heuristic that assigns Layer-0 heads to 8-bit and $k$ random non-Layer-0 heads to 2-bit, with remaining heads at 4-bit (5 seeds; we report mean$\pm$std and median);
and (5)~a naive positional heuristic that assigns Layer-0 to 8-bit and the $k$ deepest heads to 2-bit.

\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main_results}

On Qwen2.5-7B, constrained MCKP achieves 10.91 PPL, a 29.4\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45).
Without the constraint, both greedy (32.45) and MCKP (36.92) perform \emph{worse} than uniform---a catastrophic failure from excessive 2-bit assignments compounding across layers.
Across 3 calibration seeds, constrained MCKP yields mean PPL 10.99$\pm$0.06 with 90.2\% three-way allocation agreement, confirming profiling stability.

On Llama-3.1-8B, the result is essentially indistinguishable from uniform (8.45 vs.\ 8.47, $\Delta < 0.02$ PPL).
Hires profiling reveals concentration $0.57$ (comparable to Qwen's $0.61$) but a spike pattern ($t_1/t_5{=}0.85$) dominated by a single head (L2H5), leaving no cross-bitwidth gradient to exploit.

On Yi-1.5-9B, constrained MCKP ($k{=}2$) matches uniform (7.22); despite high concentration (0.71), sensitivity is dominated by a single outlier (L4H3, $t_1/t_5{=}0.90$), a spike pattern with no cross-bitwidth gradient.
On Mistral-7B-v0.3, constrained MCKP ($k{=}2$) matches uniform (7.13 vs.\ 7.13); near-zero sensitivity differences and sliding-window attention leave no room for reallocation gains.

On Gemma-2-9B$^*$ (GQA 2:1), constrained MCKP ($k{=}8$) achieves 6.20 PPL vs.\ uniform 6.17 ($+$0.4\%).
Despite flat sensitivity (concentration 0.23), unconstrained MCKP degrades to 8.85 ($1.47\times$ bf16) from 31.5\% 2-bit over-allocation; the constraint reduces this to 8 heads, confirming universal over-allocation prevention.

On Phi-3-medium-14B (GQA 4:1), constrained MCKP ($k{=}8$) achieves 5.81 PPL vs.\ uniform 5.80, consistent with its flat sensitivity profile (concentration 0.17); unconstrained MCKP degrades mildly to 6.07 ($1.08\times$ bf16). %exp_id=phi3_medium_constrained_mckp

Unconstrained failure severity tracks heterogeneity shape: \emph{catastrophic} on Qwen-7B ($3.3\times$ bf16, 60\% heads at 2-bit), \emph{severe} on Pythia ($1.9\times$), \emph{moderate} on Gemma-2 ($1.47\times$), and \emph{mild} on remaining models (${\sim}1.07$--$1.12\times$) including Qwen-14B ($1.12\times$, 20\% 2-bit)---the within-family contrast directly reflects shape (spread vs.\ flat).
The additive distortion assumption underlying standard MCKP formulations systematically fails at these bit-width gaps.

\paragraph{Aggressive compression.}
At higher compression (5.3$\times$), the cardinality constraint becomes valuable even for non-spread models: on Llama, constrained MCKP reduces PPL from 2643.8 (uniform 2-bit) to 57.6 (45$\times$ improvement); on Mistral, from 519.1 to 11.9 (44$\times$ improvement). The constraint's universal value emerges at aggressive compression ratios where uniform low-bit becomes insufficient (Appendix~\ref{sec:budget_sweep}).

See Appendix~\ref{sec:allocation_appendix} (allocation visualization) and Appendix~\ref{sec:budget_sweep} (budget sweep) for additional detail.

MCKP consistently outperforms random L0-constrained allocation and naive positional baselines across all three tested models (median gap 5--16\%; Table~\ref{tab:heuristic} in Appendix~\ref{sec:heuristic_appendix}).

\paragraph{Comparison with KIVI.}
KIVI~\cite{liu2024kivi} uses asymmetric per-channel quantization with per-token scaling, applied uniformly across all heads.
At 4-bit ($r{=}0$), KIVI achieves near-lossless PPL (9.91 on Qwen, 8.14 on Llama vs.\ 9.81/8.09 bf16), while our symmetric scheme yields 15.45 and 8.47---a gap from the quantization method, not allocation.
Within the symmetric scheme, constrained MCKP reduces Qwen from 15.45 to 10.91 ($-$4.54 PPL) by reallocating bits across heads; on Llama (spike), the gain is negligible ($-$0.02).
The two approaches are orthogonal and composable: KIVI selects the per-channel scheme, our method selects the per-head bit-width.
However, composability does not imply additive benefit: on Qwen, KIVI+MCKP achieves 9.90 PPL---identical to KIVI alone (9.90; MCKP alone: 10.91), as the per-channel method subsumes the head-level reallocation signal.
Per-head allocation provides independent value in symmetric-only deployment environments---common in hardware accelerators that lack per-channel asymmetric support---where it is the sole degree of freedom for exploiting sensitivity heterogeneity.
